Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the aerodynamic “fences” on the car’s floor and reshaped the floor’s outer edge to give it a steeper angle. Those changes boost down‑force and make the car stick better through fast corners, which should help Max and Sergio get stronger grip off the line and on the high‑speed sections this weekend. In short, the tweaks aim to keep the RB18 faster and more stable on the track.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has tweaked the angle of the rear‑wing flap to better match the demands of this circuit, giving the car a more balanced rear end. The change should boost stability through fast corners and help the drivers keep the car planted when they push hard. In short, it’s a small aerodynamic tweak that could translate into better grip and a stronger finish this weekend.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has swapped to a milder front‑wing flap and a slimmer rear wing, both trimmed down to cut drag for this track’s long straights. They’ve also added a single‑element beam wing that keeps the car stable without adding extra resistance. The result is a higher top‑speed setup that should help the team stay glued to the leaders on the straight‑line sections of this weekend’s circuit.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has tweaked the airflow at the front of the car by reshaping the brake‑duct and tweaking the front‑suspension geometry, giving the car a cleaner “bite” into the on‑track air. The changes should boost front‑end grip and stability, especially in high‑speed corners, so drivers can push harder into turn‑ins and get better traction off the line this weekend. In short, a smoother airflow package means more confidence and potentially quicker lap times right out of the gate.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams have introduced a new, slimmer beam‑wing element that slots into the rear‑wing assembly for this circuit. Its reduced size cuts drag, helping the car get up to speed faster on the straights while still keeping enough down‑force for the corners. In short, the tweak should give Williams a quicker lap time and better straight‑line performance for the weekend.

Sauber / Audi.summary: Sauber’s Audi‑powered car got a fresh front‑suspension cover that smooths the airflow around the front wheels. That cleaner air boost helps the car generate a little more down‑force and reduces drag, giving the drivers extra grip in the high‑speed corners. In short, the tweak should make the car feel more planted and quicker through the weekend’s fast sections.
